message.content:
In the key of **A** the blues scale is:

| Note | Interval from previous note |
|------|-----------------------------|
| A    | —                           |
| C    | +3 semitones (minor 3rd)   |
| D    | +2 semitones (major 2nd)   |
| E♭   | +1 semitone (minor 2nd)    |
| E    | +1 semitone (minor 2nd)    |
| G    | +3 semitones (major 3rd)   |
| A    | +2 semitones (major 2nd)   |

So the **interval pattern** (in semitones) is:

```
3 – 2 – 1 – 1 – 3 – 2
```

In other words, the A blues scale consists of the notes **A, C, D, E♭, E, G**, which correspond to the intervals:

- Root → minor 3rd  
- Minor 3rd → perfect 4th  
- Perfect 4th → diminished 5th (the “blue” note)  
- Diminished 5th → perfect 5th  
- Perfect 5th → minor 7th  
- Minor 7th → octave

This pattern is the same in any key; you just shift all the notes up or down by the appropriate number of semitones.
